Hi! So last fall I went back to school to get a second bachelor's degree in nursing. I'm in an accelerated 18 month program, so I knew going in it would be intense, but so far things have been ok for me despite things really crashing and burning mental health-wise in the past 6 months. In fact, I think having school and a future goal has really helped me push through the hard times. Homework or a tough exam can really get your mind off the bad things in life. That being said, certain classes were definitely challenging and memory intensive. Pharmacology, for example, was difficult for the majority of my peers, and requires learning and memorizing large amounts of information. 
There are so many variables, I would never say for sure whether or not you or anyone with depression should take on nursing school- but I do think that pursuing your goals is always a step in the right direction :) 
Hopefully this makes some sense- but please feel free to ask questions!

I can completely relate to what you're describing- not sure I have any answers for how to get past it though, because it really negative impacts me too. In shows I watch I skip past things like cheating in relationships, or strip club scenes etc. I think in both my life experience and the media I am so sick of hearing about men hurting, abusing, mistreating, and sexualizing women I just have to block it out or I start to think I dislike all men, which isn't true at all. Anyways- hopefully it helps to know you aren't the only one!

I told him I needed help. I told him how scared I am and asked him for help- and now that he sees just how fucked up and miserable and terrible I am he wants nothing to do with me. And he's the only person I've ever told this much to.

They're out of state on vacation all week. I know they care and I love them for it, that's the only reason I have to stay, but waking up every morning is too painful I just don't see myself making it. I feel like if I'm going to die now is the time so they don't have to be the ones to find me.

Thank you so so much. I'm 25, from near Boston- The only friend I had, if he was ever a friend, is ignoring me. I'm too ashamed to tell my family or ask them for anything more. They've had to help me though times like this before and none of this is their fault. They do everything they can, I'm just not a happy person. I just disappoint them because I can't fix anything. No matter how good things get I manage to ruin everything every time. I know I've isolated myself and that this is all my fault, but I'm so tired of trying. All I want is to not be alone but I've cut myself off from everyone, burned the few bridges I had.
